name: PayPal REST API Guidelines Evaluation Rubric
description: Comprehensive style rules based on PayPal RESTful API Guidelines. These guidelines define standards for designing REST APIs following PayPal's internal best practices. Key differentiators include snake_case property naming, HATEOAS-driven API design, and structured error handling with error catalogs.

categories.name: General Guidelines
categories.evaluationPrompt: Check if API design properly encapsulates data access through service boundaries.

categories.name: HTTP Fundamentals
categories.description: HTTP methods, headers, and status codes

options.label: Pass
criteria: HTTP methods match their semantic intent

categories.evaluationPrompt: Check if HTTP methods are used according to their standard semantics. GET should be safe and idempotent, PUT should be idempotent, etc.

categories.name: Hypermedia

options.label: Pass
criteria: Links have href and rel properties

categories.evaluationPrompt: Check if API responses include HATEOAS links for navigation and state transitions.

categories.name: Naming Conventions
categories.evaluationPrompt: Check if collection endpoints use plural nouns and avoid verbs in resource names.

categories.name: URI Design
categories.evaluationPrompt: Check if URI paths include a namespace segment after the version.

categories.name: JSON Schema
categories.description: JSON Schema usage and best practices
categories.evaluationPrompt: Check if JSON schemas use draft-04 format and include the $schema property.

categories.name: JSON Types
categories.evaluationPrompt: Check if enum values are truly fixed or if string with pattern would be more appropriate.

categories.name: Error Handling
categories.evaluationPrompt: Check if error responses follow the error.json schema with name, details, debug_id, and message fields.

categories.name: API Versioning
categories.evaluationPrompt: Check if the API specification indicates its lifecycle state.

categories.name: Deprecation
categories.evaluationPrompt: Check if deprecated API elements use the x-deprecated annotation with version and replacement info.

categories.name: Compatibility
categories.evaluationPrompt: Check if API changes are backward compatible: additive, optional, and semantically consistent.

categories.name: Security
categories.evaluationPrompt: Check if API design considers security concerns like data exposure, authentication, and authorization.
